# 1 Samuel Chapter 21 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 163r–163v | **Source Image:** 1SA_021_page_001.jpg, 1SA_021_page_002.jpg

---

**21:1** And-came David to-Nob, to-Ahimelech the-priest. And-trembled Ahimelech to-meet David, and-said to-him, "Why [are]-you alone, and-no-man [is]-with-you?"

**21:2** And-said David to-Ahimelech the-priest, "The-king commanded-me a-matter and-said to-me, 'Let-no-man know anything of-the-matter upon-which I-am-sending-you and-which I-have-commanded-you.' And-the-young-men I-have-directed to-such and-such a-place.

**21:3** And-now what [is] under your-hand? Give into-my-hand five [loaves of]-bread, or whatever is-found."

**21:4** And-answered the-priest David and-said, "There-is-no common [chol] bread under my-hand, but-there-is holy bread — if the-young-men have-kept-themselves especially from-women."

**21:5** And-answered David the-priest and-said to-him, "Indeed women have-been-withheld from-us as-formerly when-I-went-out, and-the-vessels of-the-young-men [were]-holy. And-it [is] a-common way, and-how-much-more today [when it] will-be-holy in-the-vessel."

**21:6** And-gave him the-priest the-holy [bread], for there-was no bread there except the-bread of-the-Presence [lechem ha-panim], the-[bread]-removed from-before YHWH, to-set hot bread on-[the]-day of-its-being-taken.

**21:7** And-a-man from-[the]-servants of-Saul [was] there on-that-day, detained before YHWH, and-his-name [was] Doeg the-Edomite, [the]-chief of-the-herdsmen who [belonged]-to-Saul.

**21:8** And-said David to-Ahimelech, "And-is-there-not here under your-hand a-spear or-a-sword? For both my-sword and-also my-weapons I-did-not take in-my-hand, for the-matter of-the-king was-urgent."

**21:9** And-said the-priest, "The-sword of-Goliath the-Philistine, whom you-struck in-the-valley of-Elah — behold, it [is]-wrapped in-a-cloth behind the-ephod. If that you-will-take for-yourself, take [it], for there-is-no other except-it here." And-said David, "There-is-none like-it; give-it to-me."

**21:10** And-arose David and-fled on-that day from-before Saul, and-came to-Achish king of-Gath.

**21:11** And-said [the]-servants of-Achish to-him, "Is-not this David, [the]-king of-the-land? Did-not of-this-one they-sing in-the-dances, saying, 'Saul has-struck his-thousands, and-David his-ten-thousands'?"

**21:12** And-David set these words in-his-heart and-feared exceedingly from-before Achish king of-Gath.

**21:13** And-he-changed his-discernment [ta'am] in-their-eyes and-acted-madly [va-yitholel] in-their-hand, and-scratched on-[the]-doors of-the-gate, and-let-his-spittle-run-down upon his-beard.

**21:14** And-said Achish to-his-servants, "Behold, you-see a-man acting-madly. Why do-you-bring him to-me?

**21:15** Am-I-lacking madmen, that you-have-brought this-one to-act-madly upon-me? Shall-this-one come into my-house?"

**21:16** And-David went from-there and-escaped to-[the]-cave of-Adullam. And-his-brothers heard, and-all [the]-house of-his-father, and-they-went-down to-him there.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **21:1 — Nob**: The priestly city, apparently near Jerusalem. Ahimelech's trembling suggests he suspects David is in trouble.

2. **21:5 — "vessels of the young men were holy"**: David's argument about ritual purity to access the bread of the Presence. Jesus cites this episode in Mark 2:25-26 (though naming Abiathar rather than Ahimelech).

3. **21:7 — Doeg the Edomite**: His presence "detained before YHWH" may indicate a purification ritual. His role as informer will lead to the massacre of the priests in ch.22.

4. **21:13 — va-yitholel**: "Acted madly" — the hitpael of *h-l-l*. David feigns insanity as a survival strategy. The Hebrew verse numbering differs from English (MT has 16 verses; English has 15).

— EMET
